comparison: Perfect alignment on CETSA data (C9, C62, C63). Both evaluations support the cellular thermal stabilization evidence demonstrating target engagement in cells. OpenEval emphasizes correlation with in vitro binding and appropriate controls; peer reviewers note this as part of 'multifaceted' characterization with 'compelling biophysical and cellular evidence.'

Perfect alignment on future directions (C86, C87). Both evaluations support the proposed implications for therapeutic development. OpenEval describes these as 'reasonable future directions' appropriately marked as speculative; peer reviewers emphasize the work provides 'groundwork for peptide drug modalities' and 'lays a strong foundation for future developments.'

Strong alignment on in vitro ubiquitination assays (C10, C11, C64). Both support the functional inhibition data and comparison with Apcin. OpenEval notes 'concentration-dependent inhibition is clearly demonstrated'; peer reviewers describe this as providing 'groundwork for development of peptide drug modalities to inhibit degradation.' Peer review includes C65 (mechanistic explanation) while OpenEval evaluates it separately.

Strong alignment on background and contextual claims (C1-C39, C77-C79, and additional context claims). Both evaluations support the established knowledge about ubiquitin biology, APC/C structure/function, and degron recognition. OpenEval notes these are 'appropriately supported by multiple citations'; peer reviewers made no objections and affirmed relevance. Peer review R7 includes additional context claims (C69-C85) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Strong alignment on live cell degradation assays (C12, C66, C67). Both support the degradation data and inverse correlation with binding affinity. OpenEval emphasizes statistical analysis in Figure 8D; peer reviewers describe the portable degron demonstration as 'impactful.' Peer review includes C68 and C71 (mechanistic interpretation) which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Strong alignment on X-ray crystallography data (C53-C58). Both support the structural validation of binding modes and specific interactions. OpenEval notes crystal packing effects limited C-terminal observation; peer reviewers praised 'verified binding modes by elucidating the Cdc-20-peptide structures.' Peer review also includes C51-C52 and C59-C61 which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Alignment on the key finding that binding affinity predicts inhibitory activity but not degradation efficiency (C13, C14). Both evaluations support this observation. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with cited literature; peer reviewers note this is 'consistent with conclusions from other studies.' Peer review includes C15 (mechanistic speculation) which OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN in R12.

Alignment on Apcin binding to Cdc20 (C40, C7). Both support the SPR and TSA measurements demonstrating direct binding. OpenEval emphasizes KD values with error estimates; peer reviewers describe the investigation as 'comprehensive and well-executed' with 'solid and multifaceted' binding assays. Peer review R1 covers broader scope including C6 and C41-C50.

Alignment on consensus sequence analysis and SAR studies (C41-C46, C80-C81). Both support the experimental SPR/TSA data in Table 1 and Figure 3. OpenEval notes 'appropriate replicates and error estimates'; peer reviewers describe characterization as 'comprehensive and well-executed.' Peer review R1 also covers C6-C8 and C40, C47-C50 which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Alignment on Pro3 importance through mutagenesis (C47-C50). Both support the hypothesis-driven approach combining modeling and experimental data. OpenEval emphasizes 'strong evidence for the importance of Pro3'; peer reviewers note the 'comprehensive and well-executed' investigation. Peer review R1 covers broader scope including earlier claims.

Alignment on unnatural amino acid strategy (C51, C52). Both support the rational design targeting hydrophobic pocket. OpenEval emphasizes 'high-affinity binders with well-characterized binding constants'; peer reviewers praised the 'solid and multifaceted' characterization. OpenEval also includes C6 while peer review R2 covers broader structural validation (C53-C61).

Alignment on structural interpretations (C59-C61). Both support the crystallographic data analysis including electron density correlation and crystal packing effects. OpenEval describes these as 'reasonable structural interpretations'; peer reviewers affirmed with 'compelling biophysical evidence.' Peer review R2 covers broader structural scope (C51-C58).

Alignment on mechanistic explanation for peptide potency (C65). Both support the interpretation based on D-box interactions with Cdc20 and APC10. OpenEval describes this as 'mechanistically sound explanation'; peer reviewers accepted this as part of the 'groundwork for development' narrative. Peer review R4 also covers experimental inhibition data (C10, C11, C64).

Partial alignment on mechanistic speculation (C15). OpenEval rates R12 as UNCERTAIN, noting C15 and C71 are speculative and require validation; peer review R6 appears to accept the interpretation with the caveat that it was 'strengthened by additional clarifications.' This represents a subtle difference in confidence level.

Partial alignment on APC10 role speculation (C71). OpenEval evaluates C15, C71, C69, C70, C85 together as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is reasonable but requires validation; peer review R5 appears to accept the mechanistic interpretation regarding APC10's role as part of the degradation findings, though acknowledging it remains somewhat speculative.

Alignment on D-box primacy literature (C72-C76). Both support these contextual claims from cited literature. OpenEval notes these 'accurately represent cited literature' providing important context; peer reviewers made no objections to background material, implicitly affirming accuracy and relevance.

Alignment on structural integration (C82-C84). Both support the integration of recent structural data with experimental findings. OpenEval describes the structural explanation as 'reasonable inference connecting structure to observed SAR'; peer reviewers implicitly accepted this through overall affirmation of the work's quality and relevance.
